It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. div.head: ECf 32 A 14
div.ab: Huius legis autoritate Aldredus rex subito uno eodem die per uniuersum regnum Danos occidit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 656 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

div.ab: By the authority of this law King Aldred suddenly, on one and the same day, killed the Danes throughout the whole kingdom.
